verdicts.evidence: Clicked '.queue__crumb' ("Extensions") on /barn/review. URL became https://magic-closet-rancher/dashboard/barn/extensions and '.studio-home__table' rendered, so the push resolved to a real route rather than dropping silently.

'.queue__footnote' is rendered as the last child of '.queue__list' with the sparkle icon and the text "Rows lead with what the change is for, taken from its brief - not with a file count. A change with no brief says so...". Present on every load of the queue.

Drove all three Rancher product-header controls on /barn/review. The hamburger ('[aria-label="Main menu"]') expands the app-collection rail (Home, local, Cluster Management, Continuous Delivery, Editor, Virtualization Management, Base, Users & Authentication, Extensions, Global Settings, About). '[data-testid="notifications-center"]' goes aria-expanded=true and opens the notification centre listing real entries ("Verification recorded", "Come back to it", with timestamps). '[data-testid="nav_header_showUserMenu"]' goes aria-expanded=true and opens admin / Default Admin / Preferences / Account & API Keys / Log Out. The screen itself adds no header of its own; these are Rancher's, and they work on this route.

The rail renders (70px collapsed, expands on the hamburger) and navigation works: clicking Cluster Management from /barn/review went to /dashboard/c/_/manager/provisioning.cattle.io.cluster. But the Studio entry is not marked selected on this route. Read the class list of every '.side-menu .option' on three URLs: on /barn/review the Editor (Studio) item is plain 'option'; on /c/local/settings the Global Settings item is 'option active-menu-link'; on /barn/extensions the Editor item is 'router-link-active router-link-exact-active option'. There is also no docs entry anywhere in the rail or the header, and no cluster chips beyond the single 'local' selector.
verdicts.defect: The Studio/Editor rail item loses its selected state on every barn route that is not exactly /barn/extensions, because the product's nav entry is an exact router-link to STUDIO_ROUTE (editor-product.ts line 64, `to: { name: STUDIO_ROUTE }`) and Rancher marks it with router-link-exact-active only. The queue, the review-change screen and the rest of the Studio therefore render with no rail item highlighted, so the user cannot see which product they are in. Rancher's own 'active-menu-link' mechanism does the right thing for Global Settings, so the fix is a route-prefix match rather than an exact-link match. The design's docs icon and the LT1/CD2/AFT cluster chips have no counterpart in the rail at all.

verdicts.evidence: No row on /barn/review offers 'Open the brief'. Every '.queue__action' contains only an optional Deferred chip, an SBadge and one 'Review' button (dumped the action cell of all rows). `grep -rin 'Open the brief' pkg/barn/pages/review-queue.vue` is empty; the only occurrences in the product are pages/verification.vue:791 and the extensions-list row menu at pages/extensions.vue:427. There is also no notion of a blocked row here: the queue has no state other than 'has uncommitted changes' and 'does not', and no harvester-vm-quickstart-style row exists.
verdicts.defect: The queue has no blocked state and no brief action. A row whose brief is missing is rendered with a warning line ('No brief - nobody wrote down what this is for.', review-queue.vue:354-357) but still gets the ordinary 'Review' button, so the one case where the design sends the user to the brief instead sends them into the diff.

verdicts.evidence: Clicked the 'Review' button on the first row (base, default 'Oldest first' order). URL became /dashboard/barn/review/base/working, '.rc__body' rendered, and the packet shown was base's own brief ("Mid-incident an operator cannot tell a spike in node pressure apart from a slow degradation, so they open Grafana or guess."), which matches base/BRIEF.md read out of the pod.

'.queue__lede' renders under the title row: "Nothing in this list is live. Everything here is still running only in its author's preview, and you are its only reviewer, so nothing here is waiting on anybody else."

Clicked the 'Review settings' button in the queue masthead. A modal opens, but it is the editor's settings modal: title "Editor settings", body "Used to import and publish extensions to GitHub.", one 'GitHub token' field, Cancel/Save. Escape closes it. Nothing in it concerns review.
verdicts.defect: review-queue.vue:306 wires the 'Review settings' button to `showSettings = true`, which renders components/EditorSettingsModal.vue - the GitHub-token form used by the editor and the publish flow. There are no review settings in the product; the button is a relabelled shortcut to a different screen's configuration, so a user who clicks it to change how reviews behave is shown a credential field instead.

verdicts.evidence: Every row's FIRST line is '.queue__row-title' = the extension name (base, nodehealth), and the brief sentence is the SECOND line ('.queue__intent'). The design has these the other way round. There is no version and no file/criteria count anywhere in the row: the second half of the row is YOUR PART / RISK / BRANCH columns. The intent text itself is also cut: base's row reads "Mid-incident an operator cannot tell a spike in node pressure apart from a slow" - the sentence stops mid-clause because base/BRIEF.md hard-wraps that paragraph across two lines.
verdicts.defect: Two problems. (1) review-queue.vue:348-357 renders '.queue__row-title' (name) above '.queue__intent' (purpose), inverting the design, and drops the 'name . version' + file/criteria-count line entirely. (2) intentFrom() (review-queue.vue:208-225) splits the brief on '\n' and returns a single LINE, so any hard-wrapped paragraph is truncated at the wrap: base shows '...apart from a slow' and loses 'degradation, so they open Grafana or guess.'. It should join the lines of the paragraph until the next blank line or heading.

verdicts.evidence: With the default 'Oldest first' order the rows were [base, nodehealth]. Clicked '.queue__card:nth-child(2) .queue__main' - the row body, well away from the button. URL became /dashboard/barn/review/nodehealth/working and the change that opened was nodehealth's (its packet text matched nodehealth/BRIEF.md), so the row that opens is the row that was clicked. '@click' is on '.queue__card' (review-queue.vue:344) and the button uses '@click.stop', so the two do not double-fire.

Every row does show a risk pill, and it is computed from real data, not constant: riskOf(changes) (review-queue.vue:227-233) buckets `git status --porcelain | wc -l`. Proved it by driving the count - a probe extension I created with a clean tree showed 'none', and after I wrote 10 files into its working tree the same row showed 'high'; base (1 changed file) and nodehealth (2) both showed 'low'. What is missing is the reason: the RISK column contains only the pill, no rationale string anywhere in the row's DOM. And there is no blocked state, so no em-dash placeholder case exists.
verdicts.defect: The rating has no explanation. review-queue.vue:365-368 renders the SChip alone; the design pairs the rating with a one-line reason. The rating is also only a file count - it does not distinguish a 10-file docs change from a 10-file change to the extension's entry point - so a reason line would have to be derived from something more than `changes` to be worth printing.

verdicts.evidence: No row shows a waiting duration or a person. The three columns are 'YOUR PART', 'RISK' and 'BRANCH' (BRANCH shows 'main' for every row). `grep -in 'Waiting' pkg/barn/pages/review-queue.vue` matches only the tab label 'Waiting on you' and the computed `waitingOnYou`; there is no 'requester', no author and no age rendered on a card. The screen does read a real timestamp (detail.lastChange -> row.committedAt) but only uses it to sort, never to display. The one relative time it prints is the Deferred chip's tooltip, which is not this.
verdicts.defect: row.committedAt is already available on every row and the component already has an ago() helper (review-queue.vue:180-206), so a real 'Waiting <duration>' cell is a few lines away. A requester is genuinely not available - nothing in the pod records who asked for the change, and the last commit is authored by 'barn' - so the person half of this should say so rather than be invented.

verdicts.evidence: The 'YOUR PART' pill is present on every row but is a hardcoded string. review-queue.vue:360-363 is `Author and reviewer` with no binding. Dumped all rows in both tabs, across a clean row, a 1-file row, a 2-file row and a 10-file row: every one reads 'Author and reviewer'. None of the design's three values ('Code review', 'Outcome sign-off', 'Blocked') can ever appear, and the action button is likewise always 'Review'.
verdicts.defect: The column is a constant, so it carries no information and cannot match the action button in any meaningful sense. The screen's own header comment (review-queue.vue:14-18) argues this is honest because the product has one reviewer - if that is the position, the column should be dropped or moved into the lede rather than rendered per row as though it varied.

verdicts.evidence: No row ever shows a 'Sign off' action. `grep -in 'Sign off' pkg/barn/pages/review-queue.vue` is empty. The action cell (review-queue.vue:375-387) hardcodes one SButton labelled 'Review' that always pushes REVIEW_CHANGE_ROUTE with change: 'working'. There is no route to the verification screen from this page, no obs-alert-triage row, and no 'Outcome sign-off' value for 'Your part' that could select it.
verdicts.defect: The queue cannot distinguish a code review from an outcome sign-off, so the verification screen (/barn/extensions/<id>/verification) is unreachable from the review queue.

verdicts.evidence: No row carries a re-review banner. Every '.queue__card' contains exactly one '.queue__card-body' and nothing above it (dumped card innerHTML for all rows). `grep -in 'since' pkg/barn/pages/review-queue.vue` returns nothing, and there is no longhorn-capacity row. Nothing in extensions.ts records an approval, so there is no 'last approved' point to count changes from.
verdicts.defect: The product has no record of an approval - the closest stored review state is the deferral in git config `barn.review.deferred` - so there is nothing to anchor 'changes since you last approved' to.

verdicts.evidence: Follows from 11-queue-since-banner: the banner the link would live in does not exist, so there is no link. No anchor or button in any row navigates with a scope parameter; the only navigation the row does is open(row) -> REVIEW_CHANGE_ROUTE with params { extension, change: 'working' } (review-queue.vue:269-274), which carries no scope or filter.
verdicts.defect: No way to open a change scoped to 'Since my last look' from the queue, because the queue passes only the extension name and the literal change id 'working'.

verdicts.evidence: The 'Oldest first' chip opens a menu with four items: 'Oldest first | by last commit . current', 'Newest first | by last commit', 'Most changes', 'Least changes'. Drove all four and read '.queue__row-title' out of the DOM each time, against pods whose real git state I checked with kubectl (base last commit 2026-08-21T22:37, 1 changed file; nodehealth 2026-08-22T22:25, 2 changed files). Oldest first -> [base, nodehealth]; Newest first -> [nodehealth, base]; Most changes -> [nodehealth, base]; Least changes -> [base, nodehealth]. The trigger label updates to the chosen order and the menu marks it 'current'. So it sorts on the real `git log -1 --format=%cI` timestamp and the real porcelain count, not on rendered strings.

The predicate (review-queue.vue:75-77: changes === 0 && committedAt && now - committedAt < 7 days) is satisfiable and I made it fire. Created my own probe deployment barn-q11probe-extension with a git repo holding one commit and a clean tree; the tab count went 0 -> 1 and switching to it showed exactly [q11probe] while 'Waiting on you' held [base, nodehealth] - genuinely disjoint sets. aria-selected and the s-tab--selected class moved to the second tab and back. I then wrote 10 files into the probe's tree: the count went back to 0, the tab showed the SEmpty state 'Nothing signed off this week / Extensions committed in the last seven days appear here.', and the probe moved into 'Waiting on you'. Probe deleted afterwards. Count is live, not the design's hardcoded 7.

There are two tabs, not three: '.queue__tabs' renders exactly 'Waiting on you' and 'Signed off this week'. The tab was removed on purpose and the reason is written at review-queue.vue:14-18 - nothing in the product models a second reviewer, so the filter could never match and the tab carried a hardcoded zero. `grep -in 'Waiting on others' pkg/barn/pages/review-queue.vue` matches only that comment.
verdicts.defect: Deliberately deleted rather than missed. Recording it as not-implemented because the design promises the tab and a count of 2, but the deletion looks like the right call: with one reviewer the predicate has no truth condition. Worth noting the queue does drop rows on the floor in one case - an extension whose pod is not running (barn-demo-extension, scaled to 0) reports changes 0 and no commit timestamp, so it appears in neither tab and vanishes from the screen entirely.

verdicts.evidence: Loaded /barn/review: the first tab has aria-selected="true" and class 's-tab s-tab--selected', so it is the default. Its count matched the list exactly on every read - badge 2 with rows [base, nodehealth], and badge 3 with rows [base, nodehealth, q11probe] after I added a dirty probe extension. The predicate is real (changes > 0, from `git status --porcelain | wc -l` in the pod): making the probe's tree dirty moved it into this tab and cleaning it moved it out. Count is live, not the design's hardcoded 4.
